status_summary: One element is operative, one is adopted but not yet effective, one is proposed and one is related. The FCC's Second Report and Order speeding initial processing of satellite and earth station applications was published 2025-08-27 and took effect 2025-09-26 for most provisions. The broader satellite licensing overhaul, proposed 2025-12-05, was adopted on 2026-07-22 as a Report and Order (FCC 26-47, released 2026-07-23) that creates a new part 100 to replace part 25, with modular applications, a 30-day completeness decision and a presumption that rule-compliant applications serve the public interest; the order says part 25 will sunset once part 100 takes effect, and no Federal Register publication or effective date was found. On wireline deployment, a proposal adopted 2026-06-25 and published 2026-08-07 (WC Docket 25-253) would set a 120-day deadline for state and local right-of-way decisions and limit fees to a reasonable approximation of actual direct costs; comments were due 2026-09-21 and replies are due 2026-11-05, and the part read does not address federal lands. For federal lands, Interior's regulatory agenda published 2026-08-14 lists a rule on broadband and rights-of-way under 43 CFR 2800 with no scope stated, and no directive to the Bureau of Land Management or Forest Service on review timeliness was found. On funding, NTIA told a House subcommittee on 2026-06-30 that it had approved 54 of 56 BEAD final proposals under reforms that removed a fiber preference, with about $21 billion in expected savings (per a trade summary); that is a cost and technology reform of a program aimed at unserved locations, not the chapter's call to stop funding overbuilding of existing networks.

timeline.event: FCC Second Report and Order on expediting initial processing of satellite and earth station applications is published as a final rule (removes some license modification filings and outdated rules).
FCC proposed rule, Space Modernization for the 21st Century, would overhaul space and earth station licensing through a licensing assembly line to speed reviews.

Advisory Council on Historic Preservation publishes amendments extending the Broadband Program Comment, which spares listed agencies duplicative Section 106 reviews of wireless facilities already reviewed by the FCC, to 2030-09-30 and adding the Department of Veterans Affairs.

The FCC adopts a Report and Order and Further Notice (FCC 26-47, SB Docket 25-306, released 2026-07-23) creating a new part 100 for space and earth station licensing to replace part 25, with modular applications, a 30-day completeness decision and a presumption that rule-compliant applications serve the public interest; part 25 is to sunset when part 100 takes effect, and no Federal Register publication was found.

FCC proposed rule, Build America: Eliminating Barriers to Wireline Deployments, would set a 120-day shot clock and cost-based fee limits with safe harbors for state and local right-of-way approvals (adopted 2026-06-25; comments due 2026-09-21, replies 2026-11-05).
Interior's regulatory agenda lists a rule on broadband and rights-of-way under 43 CFR 2800 (RIN 1004-AF32); only the title appears in the excerpt read.
